name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
      - develop
      - feature/**
  pull_request:
  release:
    types: [published, created, edited]

# A new push to a branch (develop, or a PR's) cancels that branch's older runs of this workflow:
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Every job builds with the same floating-point contraction: fused multiply-add, contracted across
# expressions. gcc and clang get -ffp-contract=fast, since gcc's ISO -std=c++NN modes otherwise
# mean off and clang's default only fuses within one expression; x86 also needs -mfma (arm64 has
# FMA in its base instruction set, so macOS drops it). MSVC and clang-cl get /fp:contract (or
# -ffp-contract=fast) with /arch:AVX2. -O2 rather than b2's default of -O0 because it is what
# users build with and gcc does not fuse below it, and inlining=on because b2's debug variant
# otherwise adds -fno-inline. No debug symbols: nothing here reads them, and they cost memory and
# time. The CMake jobs get the same flags through CXXFLAGS.
env:
  FMA_B2: cxxflags=-mfma cxxflags=-ffp-contract=fast cxxflags=-O2 inlining=on debug-symbols=off

# b2 -l is no use as a hang detector: on POSIX it is a CPU-time rlimit that kills multithreaded
# tests, and on Windows it misfires at launch.  So the test jobs have a job-level timeout instead.
jobs:
  ubuntu-noble:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Reads the repository only; the simulator's action uses no token or secrets.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 120
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        compiler: [ g++-14, clang++-18 ]
        standard: [ c++20 ]
        suite: [ github_ci_block_1, github_ci_block_2 ]
        include:
          # C++14 is no longer tested elsewhere, but downstream libraries (e.g. Multiprecision)
          # still include our headers in C++14 mode.  Keep one job so that breaking C++14 is a
          # deliberate, announced decision rather than something that slips in unnoticed.
          - compiler: g++-14
            standard: c++14
            suite: github_ci_block_1
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: '0'
      - name: Set TOOLSET
        run: echo ${{ matrix.compiler }} | awk '/^g/ { print "TOOLSET=gcc" } /^clang/ { print "TOOLSET=clang" }' >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - name: Add repository
        continue-on-error: true
        id: addrepo
        run: sudo apt-add-repository -y "ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test"
      - name: Retry Add Repo
        continue-on-error: true
        id: retry1
        if: steps.addrepo.outcome=='failure'
        run: sudo apt-add-repository -y "ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test"
      - name: Retry Add Repo 2
        continue-on-error: true
        id: retry2
        if: steps.retry1.outcome=='failure'
        run: sudo apt-add-repository -y "ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test"
      - name: Install packages
        run: sudo apt-get install -y g++-14 clang-18 libgmp-dev libmpfr-dev
      - name: Checkout main boost
        run: git clone -b develop --depth 1 https://github.com/boostorg/boost.git ../boost-root
      - name: Update tools/boostdep
        run: git submodule update --init tools/boostdep
        working-directory: ../bo

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
